  1. 1

    Simplify 9b−4−3b+119b - 4 - 3b + 119b−4−3b+11.

    Answer choices for question 1

    Solution

    Correct answer: B

    You chose A: Reads −3b-3b−3b as +3b+3b+3b, so the two variable terms are added rather than subtracted.

    You chose C: Carries the minus in front of the 444 onto the 111111 as well, combining the constants as −4−11-4 - 11−4−11.

    You chose D: Combines every number in sight, 9−4−3+119 - 4 - 3 + 119−4−3+11, dropping the variable rather than keeping the bbb terms apart from the constants.

    The terms 9b9b9b and −3b-3b−3b share the variable part bbb, so their coefficients add; the constants −4-4−4 and 111111 combine separately. Nothing links the two families, so the answer keeps two terms.

    9b−4−3b+11=(9−3)b+(−4+11)=6b+79b - 4 - 3b + 11 = (9 - 3)b + (-4 + 11) = 6b + 79b−4−3b+11=(9−3)b+(−4+11)=6b+7

  2. 2

    Evaluate 1211/2121^{1/2}1211/2.

    Answer choices for question 2

    Solution

    Correct answer: D

    You chose A: Reads the one-half power as a division, computing 121÷2121 \div 2121÷2.

    You chose B: Takes the square root correctly and then reciprocates as well, reading a fraction in the exponent as a call for a reciprocal, which is what a minus sign does.

    You chose C: Turns the exponent upside down and multiplies, computing 121×2121 \times 2121×2.

    A one-half power is the square root, because a1/2⋅a1/2=a1a^{1/2} \cdot a^{1/2} = a^1a1/2⋅a1/2=a1. So the value is the non-negative number whose square is 121121121.

    1211/2=121=11121^{1/2} = \sqrt{121} = 111211/2=121​=11

  3. 3

    Factor 18x2+30x18x^2 + 30x18x2+30x completely.

    Answer choices for question 3

    Solution

    Correct answer: A

    You chose B: Pulls out the greatest common divisor of the coefficients but leaves the shared xxx inside the bracket.

    You chose C: Uses 333 as the numerical part although 666 divides both coefficients, so a factor of 222 stays inside.

    You chose D: Takes out only the 222 shared by the coefficients, leaving a factor of 333 inside.

    The greatest common factor is the greatest common divisor of 181818 and 303030, which is 666, times xxx at its lowest power, which is x1x^1x1.

    18x2+30x=6x⋅3x+6x⋅5=6x(3x+5)18x^2 + 30x = 6x \cdot 3x + 6x \cdot 5 = 6x(3x + 5)18x2+30x=6x⋅3x+6x⋅5=6x(3x+5)

    The terms left inside, 3x3x3x and 555, share nothing beyond 111, so nothing more can come out.

  4. 4

    Which equation is true for every value of nnn?

    Answer choices for question 4

    Solution

    Correct answer: C

    You chose A: Reads two copies added as two copies multiplied; the two sides meet only at n=0n = 0n=0 and n=2n = 2n=2.

    You chose B: Sends the outside factor to the first term only, leaving the −2-2−2 unmultiplied.

    You chose D: Cancels the 666 on top, which is a term added to nnn rather than a factor of the whole numerator.

    An equation true for every value of its variable is an identity, and the distributive law supplies one directly: the outside factor must reach both terms inside.

    7(n+2)=7⋅n+7⋅2=7n+147(n + 2) = 7 \cdot n + 7 \cdot 2 = 7n + 147(n+2)=7⋅n+7⋅2=7n+14

    Each of the other three fails at n=1n = 1n=1, where the two sides give 222 against 111, −5-5−5 against 333, and 76\tfrac{7}{6}67​ against 222.

    Solution

    You chose C: Reads the constant term of the denominator as the excluded value without dividing by the coefficient of xxx.

    5x+20=0gives5x=−20,x=−45x + 20 = 0 \quad \text{gives} \quad 5x = -20, \quad x = -45x+20=0gives5x=−20,x=−4

    Simplify 180\sqrt{180}180​.

    Answer choices for question 6

    Solution

    Correct answer: B

    You chose A: Divides the radicand by the number brought outside instead of removing a square factor, leaving 180÷6180 \div 6180÷6 underneath.

    You chose C: Moves the perfect-square factor outside the radical without taking its root.

    You chose D: Halves the radicand instead of taking a square root.

    Split the radicand into its largest perfect-square factor times what is left, then root the part that comes out cleanly. Here 180=36×5180 = 36 \times 5180=36×5.

    180=36×5=36 5=65\sqrt{180} = \sqrt{36 \times 5} = \sqrt{36}\,\sqrt{5} = 6\sqrt{5}180​=36×5​=36​5​=65​

    The leftover 555 has no square factor, so this is as far as it goes.

    Solution

    You chose D: Multiplies −3-3−3 by the −5-5−5 but not by the aaa, so the second term loses its variable.

    Answer choices for question 9

    Solution

    Correct answer: B

    You chose A: Lets the minus sign in the exponent make the value negative instead of asking for a reciprocal.

    You chose C: Swaps the roles of numerator and denominator, taking a square root and then cubing.

    You chose D: Ignores the denominator of the exponent, reciprocating 64264^2642 with no root taken.

    Write 4x+35\dfrac{4}{x} + \dfrac{3}{5}x4​+53​ as a single fraction.

    Answer choices for question 10

    Solution

    Correct answer: D

    You chose A: Adds the numerators over the product of the denominators without rewriting either fraction first.

    You chose B: Adds numerators and denominators separately, as though that were the rule for a sum of fractions.

    You chose C: Scales the second fraction up to the common denominator but leaves the first numerator unchanged.

    The least common denominator of xxx and 555 is 5x5x5x. Multiply the first fraction by 55\tfrac{5}{5}55​ and the second by xx\tfrac{x}{x}xx​, then add the numerators.

    4x+35=205x+3x5x=3x+205x\frac{4}{x} + \frac{3}{5} = \frac{20}{5x} + \frac{3x}{5x} = \frac{3x + 20}{5x}x4​+53​=5x20​+5x3x​=5x3x+20​

  11. 11

    A student rewrites 9+5m9 + 5m9+5m as 5m+95m + 95m+9, and then rewrites the term 5m5m5m as m⋅5m \cdot 5m⋅5. Which laws license those two steps, in that order?

    Answer choices for question 11

    Solution

    Correct answer: C

    You chose A: Calls a swap of two terms a regrouping, although no bracket moved in the first step.

    You chose B: Reaches for distribution although nothing was multiplied across a sum in the first step.

    You chose D: Calls the swap of a coefficient and its variable a regrouping, although only two factors are present.

    The first step exchanges the two terms of a sum, and the second exchanges the two factors of a product. Both are order changes, not regroupings, so both are commutative laws.

    9+5m=5m+9and5m=m⋅59 + 5m = 5m + 9 \quad \text{and} \quad 5m = m \cdot 59+5m=5m+9and5m=m⋅5

    An associative law would have had to move a bracket among three quantities, and there are only two in each step.

    Answer choices for question 12

    Solution

    Correct answer: A

    You chose B: Multiplies the first terms and the last terms only, dropping the two middle products.

    You chose C: Gathers the middle products as 15x+8x15x + 8x15x+8x, ignoring the sign the −4-4−4 carries.

    You chose D: Reverses which middle product is negative, gathering 8x−15x8x - 15x8x−15x.

    Every term of the first bracket multiplies every term of the second, giving four products, and the two middle ones are like terms.

    (3x−4)(2x+5)=6x2+15x−8x−20=6x2+7x−20(3x - 4)(2x + 5) = 6x^2 + 15x - 8x - 20 = 6x^2 + 7x - 20(3x−4)(2x+5)=6x2+15x−8x−20=6x2+7x−20

    Which of these is 45x3−27x245x^3 - 27x^245x3−27x2 in fully factored form?

    Answer choices for question 13

    Solution

    Correct answer: B

    You chose A: Takes 333 as the numerical part, so a shared factor of 333 is still inside the bracket.

    You chose C: Takes only one power of xxx, so the terms inside still share an xxx.

    You chose D: Pulls out the numerical greatest common factor and leaves both powers of xxx inside.

    The greatest common divisor of 454545 and 272727 is 999, and the lowest power of xxx present is x2x^2x2, so the greatest common factor is 9x29x^29x2.

    45x3−27x2=9x2⋅5x−9x2⋅3=9x2(5x−3)45x^3 - 27x^2 = 9x^2 \cdot 5x - 9x^2 \cdot 3 = 9x^2(5x - 3)45x3−27x2=9x2⋅5x−9x2⋅3=9x2(5x−3)

    Solution

    Correct answer: A

    You chose B: Reaches the correct difference but stops before pulling out the factor both terms share.

    You chose D: Subtracts the x2x^2x2 from the expansion but leaves the 4x4x4x behind, keeping 8x+128x + 128x+12.

  18. 18

    Exactly one of these equations fails for some choice of numbers. Which one?

    Answer choices for question 18

    Solution

    Correct answer: D

    You chose A: Treats any change of bracketing as suspect, although the associative law of multiplication licenses exactly this regrouping.

    You chose B: Refuses to treat a+ba + ba+b as one quantity, although the commutative law of addition applies to whole quantities as readily as to single letters.

    You chose C: Believes distribution is stated for sums only, although b−cb - cb−c is the sum b+(−c)b + (-c)b+(−c).

    The first three are the associative law of multiplication, the commutative law of addition applied to the single quantity a+ba + ba+b, and the distributive law across a difference. The fourth has no law behind it, and one triple settles that.

    a=b=c=1:1+1×1=2,(1+1)(1+1)=4a = b = c = 1: \quad 1 + 1 \times 1 = 2, \qquad (1 + 1)(1 + 1) = 4a=b=c=1:1+1×1=2,(1+1)(1+1)=4

    Multiplication distributes over addition; addition does not distribute over multiplication.

    Solution

    Correct answer: C

    You chose A: Counts all three simplified terms as copies of 7\sqrt{7}7​, although one of them has index 333.

  1. 1

    1. Two brackets opened, and one sign with further to travel than it looks . 9 points. Question 1 of 10.

    9 pts

    Two expressions are printed below.

    P=3(2w+5),Q=4(w−2).P = 3(2w + 5), \qquad Q = 4(w - 2).P=3(2w+5),Q=4(w−2).

    1. A
      Part A.

      Write PPP and QQQ again with no brackets, each in simplest form.

      Write the expression An equation or an expression is enough here. Show how you built it. 3 points

    2. B
      Part B.

      Write P−QP - QP−Q in simplest form.

      Carry your own answer forward Work from the two bracket-free forms you produced in part A, whatever they were. The credit here is for subtracting a whole expression rather than only its first term, and for gathering what is left.

      Write the expression An equation or an expression is enough here. Show how you built it. 3 points

    3. C
      Part C.

      The constant term of P−QP - QP−Q is larger than the constant term of PPP on its own, even though something was taken away. Explain what makes that happen, and state what the constant would have come to had the subtraction reached only the first term of QQQ.

      Carry your own answer forward Account for the constant your own part B produced, even if it was not the expected one. The credit is for the account of what a leading minus sign does to each term it reaches, not for a particular number.

      Explain why it works A sentence or two. Reasons, not steps. 3 points

    The answer

    Part A

    P=6w+15P = 6w + 15P=6w+15 and Q=4w−8Q = 4w - 8Q=4w−8.

    • 6w+156w + 156w+15 may be written 15+6w15 + 6w15+6w; what is not the same is 6w+56w + 56w+5, which has left the outside factor off the second term

    Part B

    P−Q=2w+23P - Q = 2w + 23P−Q=2w+23.

    • 2w+232w + 232w+23 may be written 23+2w23 + 2w23+2w; 2w+72w + 72w+7 is what comes out if the minus sign never reaches the second term

    Part C

    Subtracting QQQ subtracts its −8-8−8, and taking away a negative adds, so the constant runs 15+8=2315 + 8 = 2315+8=23. Had the minus sign stopped at the 4w4w4w, the −8-8−8 would have been carried down unchanged and the constant would have been 15−8=715 - 8 = 715−8=7.

    Worked solution

    Part A

    The outside factor reaches both terms inside, carrying each term's sign with it.

    P=3(2w)+3(5)=6w+15,Q=4(w)+4(−2)=4w−8.P = 3(2w) + 3(5) = 6w + 15, \qquad Q = 4(w) + 4(-2) = 4w - 8.P=3(2w)+3(5)=6w+15,Q=4(w)+4(−2)=4w−8.

    Neither result gathers any further, because a www term and a constant are unlike.

    Part B

    Subtracting a whole expression means adding its opposite, and the opposite reverses the sign of every term, so the −8-8−8 arrives as +8+8+8.

    P−Q=(6w+15)−(4w−8)=6w+15−4w+8=2w+23.P - Q = (6w + 15) - (4w - 8) = 6w + 15 - 4w + 8 = 2w + 23.P−Q=(6w+15)−(4w−8)=6w+15−4w+8=2w+23.

    Part C

    Subtracting an expression is adding its opposite, and the opposite of 4w−84w - 84w−8 reverses both signs:

    −(4w−8)=−4w+8.-(4w - 8) = -4w + 8.−(4w−8)=−4w+8.

    So what joins the constant 151515 is +8+8+8, and the difference carries the constant 15+8=2315 + 8 = 2315+8=23, larger than either of the constants it came from. Nothing has gone wrong: the quantity removed was itself 888 short of 4w4w4w, and returning that shortfall is what pushes the constant up.

    The answer

    Part A

    2x2+x−212x^2 + x - 212x2+x−21.

    • 2x2+1x−212x^2 + 1x - 212x2+1x−21 is the same expression written with the invisible coefficient shown; 2x2−212x^2 - 212x2−21 has lost the two middle products

    Part B

    6x2(5x+7)6x^2(5x + 7)6x2(5x+7).

    • 6x2(5x+7)6x^2(5x + 7)6x2(5x+7) only; 2x2(15x+21)2x^2(15x + 21)2x2(15x+21) and 6x(5x2+7x)6x(5x^2 + 7x)6x(5x2+7x) are true equalities that have each left a shared factor behind inside the bracket

    Part C

    In part A the law pairs every term of one bracket with every term of the other, and two against two makes four. In part B the same law, read backwards, leaves one term inside for each term of the original sum, and there were two. The four became three only afterwards, when two of them turned out to be like terms and were gathered.

    Worked solution

    Part A

    Every term of the first bracket multiplies every term of the second, which produces four products, and two of them turn out to be like terms.

    (2x+7)(x−3)=2x2−6x+7x−21=2x2+x−21.(2x + 7)(x - 3) = 2x^2 - 6x + 7x - 21 = 2x^2 + x - 21.(2x+7)(x−3)=2x2−6x+7x−21=2x2+x−21.

    Part B

    The numerical part of the factor is the greatest common divisor of 303030 and 424242, which is 666; the variable part is xxx at the lowest power present, which is x2x^2x2.

    30x3+42x2=6x2⋅5x+6x2⋅7=6x2(5x+7).30x^3 + 42x^2 = 6x^2 \cdot 5x + 6x^2 \cdot 7 = 6x^2(5x + 7).30x3+42x2=6x2⋅5x+6x2⋅7=6x2(5x+7).

    Inside the bracket, 5x5x5x and 777 share no factor beyond 111, so nothing more can come out.

    Part C

    What fixed the four. The distributive law, used twice, pairs each term of the first bracket with each term of the second, so the count is one factor's number of terms times the other's:

    (2x+7)(x−3):2×2=4 products.(2x + 7)(x - 3): \quad 2 \times 2 = 4 \text{ products}.(2x+7)(x−3):2×2=4 products.

    What fixed the two. Read the same law from right to left, ab+ac=a(b+c)ab + ac = a(b + c)ab+ac=a(b+c). The shared factor comes out front and exactly one term stays inside for each term of the original sum. The sum 30x3+42x230x^3 + 42x^230x3+42x2 has two terms, so the bracket has two.

    Why four finished as three. Gathering is a separate step that happens once the products exist. Two of them, −6x-6x−6x and 7x7x7x, share a variable part and collapse into one; the other two have nothing to pair with. The multiplying fixed the count of products, and the gathering reduced the count of terms.

    In one line

    (2x+7)(x−3)=2x2+x−21(2x + 7)(x - 3) = 2x^2 + x - 21(2x+7)(x−3)=2x2+x−21 and 30x3+42x2=6x2(5x+7)30x^3 + 42x^2 = 6x^2(5x + 7)30x3+42x2=6x2(5x+7). Four products appear in the first because the distributive law pairs each of two terms with each of two terms; two terms remain inside the bracket in the second because the same law, read backwards, leaves one term for each term of the original sum. Gathering is a later step, and it is what turns four products into three terms.

    Square the sum before comparing, not after.

A claim that an equation holds for every number is a claim about all of them at once, so a single value where the two sides disagree contradicts it directly, which is why part B closed the matter with one substitution.     Part C

    It cannot. It divides −30a2b2-30a^2b^2−30a2b2, but 18a3b18a^3b18a3b and 12a2b12a^2b12a2b each carry only one bbb, so it fits neither. To come out, a quantity must divide every term without exception: its number must divide every coefficient, and each letter it uses must appear in every term to at least that power.

    Worked solution

    Part A

    The numerical part is the greatest common divisor of 181818, 303030 and 121212, which is 666. The variable part takes each letter at the lowest power appearing in every term: aaa appears as a3a^3a3, a2a^2a2 and a2a^2a2, so a2a^2a2; bbb appears as bbb, b2b^2b2 and bbb, so bbb. The factor is therefore 6a2b6a^2b6a2b.

    18a3b−30a2b2+12a2b=6a2b(3a)+6a2b(−5b)+6a2b(2)=6a2b(3a−5b+2).18a^3b - 30a^2b^2 + 12a^2b = 6a^2b(3a) + 6a^2b(-5b) + 6a^2b(2) = 6a^2b(3a - 5b + 2).18a3b−30a2b2+12a2b=6a2b(3a)+6a2b(−5b)+6a2b(2)=6a2b(3a−5b+2).

    Inside the bracket, 3a3a3a, −5b-5b−5b and 222 share no factor beyond 111, so nothing further comes out.

    Part B

    Every term here is the opposite of the matching term of KKK, so this expression is −K-K−K. Take the same factor out with a minus sign attached, and the bracket comes back with its first term positive.

    −18a3b+30a2b2−12a2b=−6a2b(3a)−6a2b(−5b)−6a2b(2)=−6a2b(3a−5b+2).-18a^3b + 30a^2b^2 - 12a^2b = -6a^2b(3a) - 6a^2b(-5b) - 6a^2b(2) = -6a^2b(3a - 5b + 2).−18a3b+30a2b2−12a2b=−6a2b(3a)−6a2b(−5b)−6a2b(2)=−6a2b(3a−5b+2).

    Multiplying back out returns each printed term, which is the check that the signs are right.

    Part C

    Test the candidate against each term in turn.

    −30a2b26a2b2=−5,18a3b6a2b2=3ab,12a2b6a2b2=2b.\frac{-30a^2b^2}{6a^2b^2} = -5, \qquad \frac{18a^3b}{6a^2b^2} = \frac{3a}{b}, \qquad \frac{12a^2b}{6a^2b^2} = \frac{2}{b}.6a2b2−30a2b2​=−5,6a2b218a3b​=b3a​,6a2b212a2b​=b2​.

    Only the first comes out as a term. The first and third terms of KKK carry a single bbb each, so a factor demanding two of them cannot be lifted out of either, and fitting one term out of three is not enough: the identity behind factoring, ab+ac+ad=a(b+c+d)ab + ac + ad = a(b + c + d)ab+ac+ad=a(b+c+d), needs the same quantity present in every term before anything can be taken outside.

    The general requirement follows directly. A quantity may be taken outside a bracket exactly when it divides every term: its numerical part must divide every coefficient, and each letter it contains must appear in every term to at least the power the factor uses. That is why the greatest quantity meeting the requirement takes each letter at its lowest power across the terms, and why 6a2b6a^2b6a2b comes out of KKK while 6a2b26a^2b^26a2b2 does not.

    In one line

    K=6a2b(3a−5b+2)K = 6a^2b(3a - 5b + 2)K=6a2b(3a−5b+2), built from the greatest common divisor 666 of the three coefficients together with each letter at its lowest power, a2a^2a2 and bbb. The opposite expression factors as −6a2b(3a−5b+2)-6a^2b(3a - 5b + 2)−6a2b(3a−5b+2). The candidate 6a2b26a^2b^26a2b2 cannot come out, because the first and third terms of KKK carry only one bbb each: a quantity may be taken outside a bracket only when it divides every term, which is exactly why the greatest common factor uses each letter at its lowest power.

    Rubric

    Mark your own paper against this. Give yourself the points for each element you actually wrote down, not the ones you meant to.

    Part A 5 points

    2

    Takes the numerical part to be the greatest common divisor of all three coefficients, not of two of them. . Worth 2 points.

    2

    Takes each letter at the lowest power appearing in every term, and includes no letter that is missing from a term. . Worth 2 points.

    1

    Leaves a three-term bracket whose terms share no factor beyond 111. . Worth 1 point.

    Part B 4 points

    2

    Pulls out a factor carrying a minus sign, so the bracket opens with a positive term. . Worth 2 points.

    2

    Gets the sign of every term inside the bracket right, so that the printed expression is what the factorization multiplies back out to. . Worth 2 points.

    Part C 6 points

    3

    Rejects the candidate by testing it against every term rather than only the one it fits, naming the terms it fails on and why. . Worth 3 points. needs an explanation, not just an answer

    2

    States the general requirement as dividing every term, covering both the numerical part and the power of each letter. . Worth 2 points. needs an explanation, not just an answer

    1

    Connects that requirement back to why the greatest common factor takes each letter at its lowest power. . Worth 1 point.

Marking rubrics

Work every question first. Then mark your own paper against these, giving yourself the points for each element you actually wrote down.

1. Two brackets opened, and one sign with further to travel than it looks 9 points

Part A 3

  • Multiplies the outside factor against both terms of each bracket, keeping the sign of the second term. 2
  • Leaves each answer as two terms, recognising that a variable term and a constant do not combine. 1

Part B 3

  • Reverses the sign of every term of the expression being subtracted, not only of the first. 2
  • Gathers the like terms of the result, leaving nothing further to combine. 1

Part C 3

  • Locates the rise in the fact that subtracting a whole expression reverses the sign of each of its terms, so a negative constant arrives positive. 2
  • States the constant that the truncated subtraction would have produced. 1

  • Adds the coefficients of the matching radical and leaves the radicand itself untouched. 1

  • Explains both why the result is positive and why it is greater than 111, arguing from what a negative exponent does to the base. 2
